To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the size effect in quasibritte materials is non-statistical, is described by the size effect law of fracture mechanics (SEL), is independent of the size of the weakest element, and is caused by the size-dependent strength of the weakest link.
the SEL, as formulated by Bazant, is applicable to all quasibrittlematerials, that the SEL is the most accurate size effect law for concrete, and that the BEM is the least accurate size effect law.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanics of failure of structures made of quasibritlle materials, which are characterized by a large characteristic length.
the mechanics and statistics of structural failure.
the mechanics of fracture and damage of heterogeneous solids, with the aim of developing a general framework of quasibrittlement.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the BEM is an incorrect, misleading and unnecessary model, and that the SEL based on asymptotics is the proper model for quasibrittic materials.
the BEM is a flawed model, which should not be used in practice, or in teaching, or in scientific research.
the BEM is a failed model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have been trying for decades to make a difference in the way that quasibrittile structures are designed.

the SEL based on asymptotics of quasibrittic fracture mechanics, and the cohesive crack model are the most reliable tools for predicting the strength of quasibritte structures and materials, and for assessing the safety of their designs.
, for quasibrittile materials, the size effect on strength is a fundamental property, and the SEL is a fundamental law.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the quasibrittleness of a material is not a matter of choice but a matter of fact, and that it must be recognized and dealt with, not ignored, denied or circumvented, in the design of all structures made of quasibrittable materials.
the quasibrittleness of all materials, including concrete, is the key to understanding the size effect and its proper mathematical formulation.
the BEM, as well as other SEL formulations based on the fictitious crack model, is not a viable option for design codes.
